source_text: Καὶ καθάπερ ὁ Γολιὰθ τῷ οἰκείῳ ξίφει τὴν κεφαλὴν ἀπετμήθη, οὕτω καὶ ὁ διάβολος θάνατον γεννήσας, διὰ θανάτου τροποῦται· καὶ τὴν εὐχερῆ μέθοδον τῆς οἰκείας ἀπάτης, ὄργανον ἰσχυρὸν τῆς ἰδίας ἀπωλείας εὑρίσκει· καθάπερ ἄγκιστρον περιπαρεὶς τῇ Θεότητι, καὶ τὸ σύνηθες δέλεαρ καταπιὼν ἀγρεύεται σαφῶς ὁ ἀγρεύειν οἰόμενος· καὶ Θεὸν ἀντὶ ἀνθρώπου κρατήσας. Διὰ τοῦτο μάρτυρες σκιρτῶσιν τὴν τοῦ δράκοντος κεφαλήν· καὶ πᾶν εἶδος βασάνων ὑπερορῶσιν. Ἀφ' οὗ γὰρ ὁ δεύτερος τὸν πρῶτον Ἀδὰμ ἐκ τοῦ πυθμένος τοῦ ᾅδου ὡς τὸν Ἰωνᾶν ἐκ τοῦ κήτους ἀνήγαγεν, καὶ τὸν ἀπατηθέντα, εἰς ἐντροπὴν τοῦ ἀπατήσαντος, οὐρανοπολίτην ἀνέδειξεν· ἐξ ἐκείνου πύλαι ᾅδου ἐκλείσθησαν· καὶ πύλαι οὐρανοῦ ἀνεῴχθησαν· ἀκώλυτον τοῖς μετὰ πίστεως ἀνιοῦσιν παραχωροῦσαι τὴν εἴσοδον. Πάλαι μὲν Ἰακὼβ κλίμακα ἐστηριγμένην ἕως τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἐθεάσατο, καὶ τοὺς ἀγγέλους τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀναβαίνοντας καὶ καταβαίνοντας· νυνὶ δὲ διὰ τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἄνθρωπος γενόμενος ὁ φιλάνθρωπος τὸν ἀπάνθρωπον λακτίσας τῷ ποδὶ τῆς θεότητος, καὶ τὸν ἄνθρωπον βαστάσας τῇ χειρὶ τῆς χριστότητος, τὸν ἄβατον αἰθέρα ποσὶν ἀνθρωπίνοις πεζεύσασθαι παρεσκεύασεν. Τότε οἱ ἄγγελοι ἀνέβαινον καὶ κατέβαινον· νυνὶ δὲ ὁ τῆς μεγάλης βουλῆς Ἄγγελος οὐκ ἀναβαίνει καὶ καταβαίνει· καὶ πόθεν γὰρ ποῦ μεταστήσεται ὁ πανταχοῦ παρών, καὶ τὰ πάντα πληρῶν, καὶ ἐν τῇ χειρὶ συνέχων τὰ [κόσμου] πέρατα; Ἅπαξ γὰρ κατέβη καὶ ἅπαξ ἀνέβη· οὐ μεταβάσει χρησάμενος φύσεως, ἀλλὰ συγκαταβάσει φιλανθρώπου χριστότητος· ὁ Λόγος τῷ Πατρὶ συγκαθήμενος, καὶ ὁ Λόγος ἐν τῇ μήτρᾳ αὐλιζόμενος, καὶ ὁ Λόγος πανταχοῦ εὑρισκόμενος, καὶ [τοῦ] τῶν ὅλων [Θεοῦ] μηδέποτε χωριζόμενος.
thought_title: The devil caught on his own hook, and heaven opened
orientation: The devil, who brought death into being, is undone by death: swallowing the bait of Christ's humanity, he is caught on the hook of His Godhead. Christ brings Adam up from Hades, shuts its gates, opens heaven, and, unlike the angels on Jacob's ladder, comes down and goes up without ever leaving any place, for He fills all things.
pass_a_gloss: And just as Goliath was cut off as to the head by his own sword, so also the devil, having begotten death, through death is routed; and the easy method of his own deceit he finds a strong instrument of his own destruction; as a hook having been pierced/impaled on the Godhead, and having swallowed down the accustomed bait, he who thought to catch is clearly caught, having seized God instead of a man. Because of this martyrs leap the head of the dragon [bare accusative: leap upon/over], and every form of tortures they disdain. For from when the second [Adam] led up the first Adam from the bottom of Hades, as Jonah from the sea monster, and the deceived one, for the shame of the deceiver, displayed as a heaven-citizen; from that [time] the gates of Hades were shut and the gates of heaven were opened, granting unhindered entrance to those going up with faith. Of old Jacob beheld a ladder fixed up to heaven, and the angels of God going up and coming down; but now, for the sake of man having become man, the man-loving one, having kicked the inhuman one with the foot of the Godhead, and having carried the man with the hand of kindness/goodness, prepared [that] the untrodden upper air be walked on foot with human feet. Then the angels were going up and coming down; but now the Angel of the great counsel does not go up and come down; for from where to where will he change place, the one everywhere present, filling all things, and holding together in the hand the ends [of the world, bracketed in print]? For once he came down and once he went up, not having used a passing-over/change of nature, but a condescension of man-loving kindness; the Word seated together with the Father, and the Word lodging in the womb, and the Word found everywhere, and never separated from [the God] of all things.

choices.english: Impaled on the Godhead as on a hook
choices.why: περιπείρω is 'pierce, impale'; the image is a fish caught on the hook hidden in the bait of Christ's humanity.
rejected: Caught on the hook of the Godhead

choices.why: Intransitive verb with a bare accusative, confirmed on the page image; 'leap upon' keeps the trampling sense without adding a verb.

choices.english: the Lover of mankind ... the enemy of mankind
choices.why: Keeps the ἄνθρωπος wordplay visible in English while making clear that ἀπάνθρωπος names the devil.
rejected: the humane one ... the inhuman one

choices.why: Lexical sense 'kindness, goodness'; the play on Christ's name cannot be kept and is explained in a note.

choices.term: οὐ μεταβάσει χρησάμενος φύσεως, ἀλλὰ συγκαταβάσει
choices.english: not by any shift of His nature, but by the condescension
choices.why: Keeps the contrast of μετάβασις and συγκατάβασις and the negation exactly.
rejected: not by passing from His nature

choices.english: never separated from the God of all
choices.why: Follows the print's editorial supplements; the unsupplemented reading is recorded in the translator notes.

pass_b_english: Just as Goliath had his head cut off with his own sword (1 Samuel 17:51), so too the devil, who gave birth to death, is routed through death. He finds that the easy method of his own deceit is a strong instrument of his own destruction. Impaled on the Godhead as on a hook, having swallowed the familiar bait and seized God instead of a man, the one who thought he was catching is plainly caught.

This is why martyrs leap upon the dragon's head and look down on every kind of torture. For from the time the second Adam brought the first Adam up from the depths of Hades (1 Corinthians 15:45–47), as He brought Jonah up from the sea monster (Jonah 1:17–2:10), and to the shame of the deceiver made the deceived a citizen of heaven, from that time the gates of Hades have been shut and the gates of heaven opened, granting unhindered entrance to those who go up in faith.

Long ago Jacob saw a ladder set up and reaching to heaven, and the angels of God going up and coming down (Genesis 28:12). But now the Lover of mankind, who became man for the sake of man, has kicked the enemy of mankind with the foot of the Godhead, has carried man in the hand of His kindness, and has made it possible to walk the untrodden heights of the sky on human feet.

Then the angels went up and came down; but now the Angel of Great Counsel (Isaiah 9:6) does not go up and come down. For from where, and to where, would He move, who is present everywhere, who fills all things, and who holds the ends of the world in His hand (Psalm 95:4)? For He came down once and went up once, not by any shift of His nature, but by the condescension of His kindness and love for mankind: the Word seated with the Father, the Word dwelling in the womb, the Word found everywhere, and never separated from the God of all.
notes: Goliath beheaded with his own sword: 1 Samuel 17:51 (LXX 1 Kingdoms 17:51).
'Second Adam ... first Adam' is cited to 1 Corinthians 15:45-47, where Paul speaks of the first and last Adam, the first and second man.
Jonah raised from the sea monster: Greek and Hebrew Jonah 2:1-11 is English Jonah 1:17-2:10; cited in English numbering.
The verb ἀνήγαγεν governs both Adam and Jonah, so the one who brought Adam up is also the one who brought Jonah up ('as He brought Jonah up').
Jacob's ladder with the angels going up and coming down: Genesis 28:12.
'Angel of Great Counsel' (ὁ τῆς μεγάλης βουλῆς Ἄγγελος) is Isaiah 9:5 in the Septuagint, Isaiah 9:6 in English Bibles (the 'Wonderful Counselor' verse); cited in English numbering.
'Holds the ends of the world in His hand' echoes Psalm 94:4 in the Septuagint (ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ τὰ πέρατα τῆς γῆς), which is Psalm 95:4 in English Bibles; cited in English numbering.

σκιρτῶσιν τὴν τοῦ δράκοντος κεφαλήν uses an intransitive verb with a bare accusative; the page image confirms the printed reading, rendered 'leap upon the dragon's head'. A possible echo of Psalm 91:13 (LXX 90:13, trampling the dragon) or Genesis 3:15 is left uncited as uncertain.

Allusions left uncited as uncertain: 'gates of Hades' (Matthew 16:18, though the sermon uses the phrase in a different sense), 'citizen of heaven' (Philippians 3:20), 'fills all things' (Ephesians 4:10; Jeremiah 23:24), and 'came down once and went up once' (John 3:13; Ephesians 4:9-10).
The wordplay ἄνθρωπος / φιλάνθρωπος / ἀπάνθρωπος is rendered 'man ... Lover of mankind ... enemy of mankind'; ἀπάνθρωπος is literally 'the inhuman one', meaning the devil.

χριστότης ('kindness, goodness', with a play on Christ's name) is rendered 'kindness' both times; φιλανθρώπου χριστότητος is rendered 'His kindness and love for mankind' to keep φιλάνθρωπος visible. The play on Christ's name cannot be kept in English.
αἰθήρ ('upper air') is rendered 'heights of the sky'. μετάβασις φύσεως ('a passing over, a change of nature') is set against συγκατάβασις ('condescension'); rendered 'not by any shift of His nature'.

The print's editorial brackets [κόσμου] and [τοῦ] ... [Θεοῦ] are translated as part of the text ('of the world', 'the God of all') without brackets in the reading column. Without the bracketed supplements the last clause would read 'never separated from all things' (τῶν ὅλων).
Capitalised pronouns (He, His) mark Christ, to keep Him distinct from the devil in this passage.
